bom.function: Right-angle SMD tactile button (Würth), one on each side of the board. One is wired to /RESET and the other to /BTN_LOCK, so they are Reset and Lock. Page turning uses the seven front buttons.
Right-angle SMD slide switch (C&K, SPDT). Power on/off slide switch on the device side.
Dual AAA battery holder (Keystone). SMD-mounted; the 1022C retainer clip is required separately to keep cells in place.
Retainer clip for the Keystone 1022 battery holder. Snaps over installed AAA cells.

P-channel MOSFET, two on the board. Q1 sits in the battery power path (gate VBUS, source VCC, drain +BATT). Q2 switches the +3.3VP rail: gate /~{EN2} (Pico GPIO0), source +3V3, drain +3.3VP. That rail powers the C2 module and the chip-select pull-ups.
10 µF MLCC, 1206, ≥6.3 V. Bulk decoupling on the battery rail (+BATT) and the switched 3.3 V rail (+3.3VP).
1 µF MLCC, 0805, ≥6.3 V. Local decoupling on the 3V3 rail.
10 kΩ, 1206. R3 pulls the flash chip select (/BABEL_CS) up to +3.3VP. R4 does the same for the microSD chip select (/SD_CS).

The MCU. Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 @ 133 MHz, 264 KB SRAM, 2 MB onboard flash). Runs the libros firmware. This is the original Pico (SC0915), the non-wireless board the firmware's `board = pico` setting names.
Push/push microSD card slot. Holds the book library on a microSD card — UTF-8 .txt files with support for bold, italic, chapter breaks, and front-matter metadata via inline control codes.
16 Mb SPI NOR flash. Stores the GNU Unifont + per-language glyph data that doesn't fit in the Pico's 2 MB flash. Read over the shared SPI bus via /BABEL_CS.

offers.note: Listed as Not For New Designs. Do not swap in a similar chip without checking package, electrical behavior and firmware support.

bom.function: 3 × 6 mm through-hole tactile button (E-Switch). The menu / directional / select cluster under the screen. 7 placements (B3–B9). The BOM specifies the 180WQ (1.8 N, firmer click); the upstream README links to the 130WQ (1.3 N, lighter touch). Either fits the same footprint — order whichever feel you prefer.
3-pin JST PH SMD connector (STEMMA style), J1 and J2. OPTIONAL expansion. Each carries one GPIO signal, +3V3 and GND.
4-pin JST SH SMD connector (STEMMA QT style), J3. OPTIONAL expansion. Pins are RX/SCL, TX/SDA, +3V3 and GND, so it can serve as an I²C port.
1 kΩ, 0805. OPTIONAL. R1 and R2 are series resistors between the Pico's GP26 and GP27 and the expansion connector signals. Fit them only if the expansion ports are used.

bom.description: Oddly Specific castellated E-paper driver module
bom.function: Castellated e-paper driver submodule. Generates the ±22 V and ±15 V rails the e-paper panel needs, converts signal levels between the Pico and the display, and drives the FFC ribbon. Ordered pre-assembled from JLCPCB or PCBWay; soldered to the C1 main board via castellated edge pads.

bom.description: 4.2 Inch B&W E-paper Panel (unvalidated; stock unconfirmed)
bom.function: 4.2-inch B&W e-paper panel (Good Display), 400 × 300 px, SSD1683 controller, 24-pin FFC to the C2 driver module. Unvalidated in this design: see the notes. Order the black and white model, not the tri-colour one.

offers.note: Two Good Display listings showed zero stock. An earlier search excerpt showed $14.96. Not a confirmed basket for ten panels.

bom.function: 0.47 Ω sense resistor, 0603. Current-sense feedback for the boost converter that generates the e-paper high-voltage rails.
10 µH inductor, 0805, 500 mA. Energy storage for the boost converter.

bom.description: 1uF ±10% 50V X7R 0805 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT RoHS
bom.function: 1 µF MLCC, 0805, 50 V, X7R. Bypass and filter capacitors throughout the driver circuit (9 placements).

bom.description: 4.7uF ±10% 25V X5R 0805 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT RoHS
bom.function: 4.7 µF MLCC, 0805, 25 V, X5R. Bulk decoupling on the driver power rails.

bom.description: Contact,Top 24 0.020"（0.50mm） 0.079"（2.00mm） Slide Lock 24P FFC, FPC Connectors RoHS
bom.function: 24-pin 0.5 mm FFC connector. Connects the flat flex cable from the e-paper display panel.
N-channel MOSFET, 100 V, 1.6 A, SOT-23. Switches the e-paper gate driver voltage rail.
30 V Schottky diode, SOD-123. Charge-pump rectifiers for the negative voltage rails (3 placements).

assembly.title: Order the C1 main board (bare PCB) and the C2 e-paper driver (pre-assembled module)
assembly.description: Order two things. C1: upload OSO-BOOK-C1-05-rounded.zip to a PCB maker (two layers, 1.0 mm thick, lead-free HASL or ENIG). C2: order the driver as a finished module from the C2-03 package for JLCPCB (BOM, placement file and Gerbers from the same folder; castellated edges, 1.0 mm, lead-free HASL). Order the display, the Pico (original SC0915) and the other parts from the Parts list. See the Checklist tab for the full list.
assembly.notes: The C1 zip holds Gerbers and drill files only. It has no placement file or assembly-ready BOM, so a factory cannot assemble C1 from it alone. Ask each maker for a quote that names the exact package, quantity, finish and which parts they place. Nothing has been ordered or quoted yet.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount (SMD) passives on C1: 10 µF, 1 µF, 10 kΩ (and optionally 1 kΩ)
assembly.description: Start with the smallest surface-mount passives. C1 and C2 are 10 µF 1206 caps. C3 is a 1 µF 0805 cap. R3 and R4 are 10 kΩ 1206 resistors. If you want the STEMMA expansion, also install R1 and R2 (1 kΩ 0805). These take flux and a fine tip but don't require hot air.
assembly.notes: R1/R2 are OPTIONAL — install them if you plan to use the STEMMA/I²C expansion ports.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount chips on C1: flash chip and MOSFETs
assembly.description: U4 is the GD25Q16C 16 Mb flash chip (SOIC-8, an 8-pin chip package). Q1 and Q2 are P-channel DMG3415U-7 MOSFETs (SOT-23, a 3-pin chip package). Use flux and drag-solder technique (run the iron tip slowly across all pins at once) for U4; Q1/Q2 are 3-pin, easy one-pin-at-a-time.
assembly.notes: Watch Q1/Q2 orientation — the DMG3415U-7 is P-channel.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount connectors and switches on C1: µSD slot, side buttons, slide switch
assembly.description: U3 is the GCT MEM2075 microSD push/push slot (fine-pitch metal shell — solder the shell tabs first for alignment). B1 and B2 are Würth right-angle tactile buttons. SW1 is the C&K power slide switch. Install the optional J1/J2/J3 JST connectors in this step too if you're using expansion.
assembly.notes: The SD slot has both signal pins and shell tabs — tack the shell tabs first to prevent the slot from shifting while you solder the signal pins.

assembly.title: Solder the Keystone 1022 battery holder + 1022C retainer clip on C1
assembly.description: BT1 is the dual-AAA battery holder (surface-mount through-pad). These pads draw heat — use a larger tip and extra flux. Install the 1022C retainer clip, which physically retains the AAA cells.
assembly.notes: The 1022C retainer clip is easy to miss — make sure you've ordered it (Digi-Key 36-1022C-ND).

assembly.title: Solder the C2 e-paper driver module onto C1 via castellated edges (the row of half-circle pads along the board edge)
assembly.description: U2 is the pre-assembled Castellated E-Paper Driver. Drop it into its footprint on the main board and solder the castellated pads. The module generates the ±22 V and ±15 V rails the e-paper needs.
assembly.notes: The C2 internals were assembled at the fab house. Solder the castellated edge pads to the matching C1 pads beneath.

assembly.title: Solder the 7 through-hole tactile buttons on C1 (B3–B9)
assembly.description: The menu / directional / select cluster under the screen: 7× TL1107AF180WQ. Install from the front of the board; solder on the back. Push buttons face outwards (away from the PCB).
assembly.notes: These are gullwing-style — make sure the tactile switch body seats flat against the board before soldering. Note: the BOM specifies TL1107AF180WQ (1.8 N, firmer click) but the README links to 130WQ (1.3 N, lighter touch). Either fits the same footprint.

assembly.title: Solder the Raspberry Pi Pico (U1) onto C1
assembly.description: The Pico can be installed in two ways: through-hole pin headers (if you want it removable for reflashing) or reflowed via its castellated edge pads (flush, permanent). The castellated method gives the slimmest profile.
assembly.notes: Pin headers make reflashing easy if you plan to iterate on firmware. Castellated gives the slimmest profile for a finished device.

assembly.title: Attach the e-paper panel via FFC (flat ribbon cable) to the C2 module
assembly.description: Slide the panel's flexible tail into the 24-pin 0.5 mm FFC connector on the C2 module with the contacts facing the right way, then close the latch. Handle the panel by its edges and keep it supported while the board is on the bench.
assembly.notes: The panel is the GDEY042T81. Pair it only with firmware that supports its SSD1683 controller (libros PR #11). The C2 inductor, current-sense resistor and pulldown values for this panel are unconfirmed, so treat the first unit as a pilot.

assembly.title: Prepare the microSD card (fonts first, then a short book)
assembly.description: Format a microSD card as FAT32 on your Linux computer. Copy babel.bin (the font data) to the card root, then add one short UTF-8 .txt book: the first line is the title. Do this before the first boot so the firmware can load the fonts.
assembly.notes: Use one known card and filesystem for the pilot and write down which. The old note that any capacity works was not verified. Formatting codes, front matter and the libros-convert tool are described at https://oddlyspecificobjects.com/projects/openbook/ (a 2022 page).

assembly.title: Build the libros firmware with PlatformIO and flash the Pico
assembly.description: On Linux, install PlatformIO, clone joeycastillo/libros, apply the two community fixes (PR #10 removes a stray pico/stdlib.h include; PR #11 selects the display driver at runtime), and run `platformio run -e pico`. To flash, hold BOOTSEL on the Pico while plugging in USB; it appears as a drive. Copy the .uf2 onto it and the Pico restarts into libros.
assembly.notes: The libros PlatformIO environment is `pico` (platform raspberrypi, board pico, Arduino framework, picotool upload). PR #10 and PR #11 were open and unmerged on 2026-11-15, and nobody has built or run the two together yet. The prebuilt book.uf2 targets the older GDEW042T2 display only.

assembly.title: First boot: the firmware copies the fonts into the flash chip
assembly.description: Put the prepared microSD card in the slot and power the reader. On first boot the firmware copies babel.bin from the card into the external GD25Q16C flash chip (U4). Wait for it to finish, then check that text renders.
assembly.notes: babel.bin holds GNU Unifont data for the Unicode Basic Multilingual Plane. The old instruction to flash it with a bootloader utility is not how the Pico build works.

assembly.title: 3D-print the case and assemble (deferred)
assembly.description: Print 'Open Book Abridged - Minimal Case.stl' from the upstream repo's 3D Printed Case directory (https://github.com/joeycastillo/The-Open-Book/tree/main/3D%20Printed%20Case). The STL prints support-free on any FDM printer. Fit the completed board, insert 2× AAA batteries, and close the case.
assembly.notes: Cases are out of scope for the first ten readers. The case is designed for a 1.0 mm board.
